clue.text: Warning help will be needed for action in court

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shouted warning
a hand is help, as in 'lend a hand'

explanation.surface: A legal warning that assistance will be required for a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a law court, but it is a tennis court, and the action is a stroke played there.
explanation.definitionFit: A forehand is a stroke played on a tennis court, palm facing forward.

indicators.note: sin goes around the letter, so 'about' signals a container

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

indicators.note: 'first' takes only the opening letter of the director's name

explanation.surface: Something improper about the debut picture of Alexander Korda, the film producer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like a cinema film, but it means a thin layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin is a thin surface layer, as on custard or boiled milk.
Orders are kinds or classes (the lower orders) and also commands given to be obeyed.
Variance is a change or deviation, and being at variance means being in disagreement.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'with New Testament (10)': the opening words are missing from the newspaper text and no source gives the full clue.

indicators.note: 'into' places the escorted word inside the word for very

parts.note: too means very, as in 'not too bad'
to lead someone is to escort them, so escorted gives led

explanation.surface: Someone was escorted deep into a Spanish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Toledo is a historic city in central Spain, famous for its swords.

clue.text: Time in the morning to make a stack at brag?

parts.note: to cock hay is to pile it into a small conical stack
to crow is to boast

explanation.surface: A question about the hour for building a big pile of chips in the card game brag.
explanation.walkthrough: Brag is a British card game, so 'stack' looks like a pile of chips; here 'brag' is just a verb meaning boast.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn is when the rooster calls, so the early hour is named after that call.

parts.note: a hippy was a 1960s drop-out from conventional society

explanation.surface: A question about an electrical switch fitted with a fallout feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch' suggests an electrical switch, but it is a thin flexible stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A switch is a slender bendy cane, so it is flexible like a lash.
Soldiers in action are in combat, and an action is also a movement of the body, such as a gesture.

indicators.note: the word for knowledge goes about the letter for English, a container

parts.note: ken is knowledge, as in 'beyond my ken'

explanation.surface: Keen to learn about the English language.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone keen is enthusiastic and impatient to do something.

indicators.note: roughly suggests the letters are handled crudely and rearranged

explanation.surface: A lazy prisoner was dragged out of the cell.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eliminated has been got rid of or taken out of contention.

clue.text: This insect or another is found on Malta

indicators.note: 'found on' puts the other pieces after the letter for Malta, as if resting on it

parts.note: M is the international vehicle code for Malta
another insect, here the ant

explanation.surface: A remark that this insect, or a different one, lives on the island of Malta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' stands for a second insect, the ant.
explanation.definitionFit: The praying mantis is a predatory insect that holds its forelegs as if in prayer.

clue.text: River clogged with crude endless lumber from plant

indicators.note: the river is clogged, so another word is packed inside it

parts.note: the Tweed is a river on the English-Scottish border

indicators.note: crude means rough and unrefined, so the letters are reworked
'endless' cuts the last letter from the word lumber

explanation.surface: A river choked with rough timber that came from a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' removes R from LUMBER; 'crude' rearranges LUMBE to UMBLE, which goes into TWEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumbleweed is a plant that breaks off and rolls across open plains in the wind.

parts.note: to broach is to pierce, so it means punch

indicators.note: new indicates the letters of 'one' are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Open up a fresh barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broach' and 'cask' go together naturally (broaching a cask means tapping it), but 'Broach' gives PUNCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A puncheon is a large barrel for liquids such as rum or wine.

indicators.note: cultivated suggests the letters are worked over like soil

explanation.surface: Fruit grown by wandering people.
explanation.definitionFit: A damson is a small dark purple plum.
Rules that were kept were obeyed, and something seen or perceived was noticed.

clue.text: Restful piece without a hint of dissonance

indicators.note: 'without' drops the letters that follow it from the musical piece

parts.note: a serenade is a piece of music

indicators.note: a hint of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A calming piece of music with no trace of discord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes A and D (first letter of 'dissonance') from SERENADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Serene means calm and peaceful, untroubled.

clue.text: Third cell, almost abandoned, is eerie

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and uncontrolled, so the letters are rearranged
'almost' cuts the final letter of the word cell

explanation.surface: A third prison cell, nearly deserted, feels creepy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' leaves CEL from CELL; 'abandoned' rearranges THIRD and CEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Eldritch is a Scots word for weird and unearthly.

clue.text: The Italian in front is fluent in speech

indicators.note: 'in' places the Italian article inside the front

parts.note: a face is a front, as a building's face
il is the Italian word for 'the'

explanation.surface: An Italian in front is a fluent talker.
explanation.definitionFit: Facile means smooth and ready, especially of glib talk.

clue.text: Old contraption located a stone's throw away?

definitions.text: Old contraption located a stone's throw away?

parts.words: Old contraption located a stone's throw away?
parts.note: read literally, an ancient device that throws stones a distance, rather than something nearby

explanation.surface: An antique machine found only a short distance off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A stone's throw away' normally means close by; here it describes a siege engine that hurls stones.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballista was an ancient Roman siege weapon that hurled stones or bolts.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Setter for Independent re-set leader (6)': LEADER has one L and two Es, so no anagram gives the answer, and no source gives the printed clue or the setter's intent.

clue.text: Happen debit's wrongly calculated to a point

indicators.note: a sum wrongly calculated has its figures in the wrong order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter
E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A debit miscalculated to the decimal point might happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' links the anagram of DEBIT to E.
explanation.definitionFit: Betide means to happen or befall, as in 'woe betide'.

clue.text: Officer in drink proves excellent type

indicators.note: 'in' places the officer inside the drink

parts.note: beer is a drink
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: An officer in drink turns out to be a fine fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: A belter is British slang for something outstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: A belter is something or someone outstandingly good, informal British slang.

parts.note: girls' names that are also names of blooms

explanation.surface: Asking which of two blooms is meant.
explanation.walkthrough: The names read as plants, but they are names given to girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose and Violet are girls named after blooms; a bridesmaid who scatters petals is also so called.

indicators.note: 'without tail' cuts the last letter of the word for coat

parts.note: paint is a coat applied to a surface

explanation.surface: A coat lacking tails is stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' looks like an adjective (stylish), but it is the noun or verb sense of stinging hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: To smart is to sting, and a smart is a sharp stinging hurt.

indicators.note: 'it's said' tells you to go by how the dog's name sounds

parts.note: a peke is a Pekingese dog

explanation.surface: Top dog, as they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top dog' reads as one phrase but splits into the definition and the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A peak is the summit or highest point.

clue.text: Renounce some vague generalisation on reflection

indicators.note: on reflection means seen as in a mirror, so the run is read backwards
'some' takes a run of letters from inside the phrase

explanation.surface: Withdraw a fuzzy sweeping statement after thinking it over.
explanation.definitionFit: To renege is to go back on a promise, abandoning a commitment.

clue.text: Graceful quality, say, imbuing English cutter

indicators.note: 'imbuing' puts the example word inside the cutter, soaking into it

parts.note: a lance is a surgeon's cutting blade
eg, for example, means 'say'

explanation.surface: A refined quality, say, shown by an English blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutter' might suggest a boat, but here it is a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegance is gracefulness and refined style.
